newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug cos Q1 gains seen driven by volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug cos Q1 gains seen driven by volume.

text.p: Earnings for drug companies will show a healthy rise in the first quarter that will continue through the rest of the year, driven by volume gains that will more than offset the effect of the stronger dollar on sales abroad.
"We think that the drug stocks are going to be strong for the next couple of years," said Cynthia Beach, vice-president of Gerard Klauer Mattison.
Beach sees the higher volumes that drove last year's earnings continuing and thinks the strong dollar will hurt results minimally.
"Currency is not an issue for companies with stronger earnings," she said.
According to First Call, the consensus estimate for first quarter earnings is a rise of 12 percent for the drug group.
David Saks, senior vice president of Gruntal Investment Research, said profit margins are expanding and earnings growth is accelerating.

"Industry fundamentals are the strongest in years," Saks said. Saks noted the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved 53 new chemical entities in 1996, compared with an average of 26 per year over the past five years.
"Fifty-three is an awesome number," he said. "There is an unmet pent-up demand that jumps at good new products."

Among the drugs that obtained FDA approval in 1996 are Warner-Lambert Co's cholesterol drug Lipitor and Eli Lilly and Co's antipsychotic Zyprexa and Merck & Co Inc's Crixivan protease inhibitor for AIDS.
Beach said that prescription volumes through managed care are increasing.
"What's driving managed care to prescribe more is the realization that the cost of a prescription now is lower than the cost of treatment later," Beach said.
